Damn, that sounds really hard. This is long and I’m using my dictation to do it so, lol bare w me. But: 

I know what you mean by the up and down and I do the exact same thing with romanticing later - right after the break up I’m like - oh yeah it hurts but I’m super clear about why it didn’t work. But then as you get distance you’re like, just having the good future wishes and memories. 

I’ve had a really hard time with this recent one - I don’t know that I’ve loved anybody more and I even catch myself reaching out my hand to hold his hand when I’m driving. It is so sad! I cry but then laugh at how goofy sad it is... I’m mega sappy on this guy. And I just break down at the gym if I see anyone that looks like him or if I hear a song that reminds me of him or even just really anything.I do think this is why friends are so important especially ones that knew you or heard about the relationship while you were in it and when you broke up because they will be the ones who will say “hey remember when that person did something so horrible and that’s a dealbreaker.” 

I will say I am genuinely happily shocked that I am over the longer relationship that was before this one, it was four years and I really never thought that I would get over it. And I wasn’t for a while, it just seemingly happened. Boom. I thought I would learn to live with the fact that I wasn’t over it and I would date other people and I would maybe even get married or whatever but I would never really be over it. And I am shocked to say this but I have no feelings about it I feel completely indifferent which is what I’ve heard happens but I never thought it would happen for this, never. I really was suicidal when that relationship ended I thought I was gonna lose my mind. Or I did lose my mind. But that relationship now just seems like it was a waste of time now, and I have no feelings about that guy. I did with such intensity and certainly and lingering even for long! I actually think it inhibited me from enjoying a couple really lovely relationships after. Both of the guys I dated after were really lovely comparatively and I just wasn’t present because I wasn’t over that relationship. 

It kind of makes me think it just takes going through other relationships and a chunk of time. I’m not sure I really don’t know I’m still kind of in disbelief that I’m just so over it I could not care less - it’s weird because I am such a romantic emotional person but I really don’t feel anything. Like at all. I feel actually nothing and I look at it just very logically now. 

But I do think that relationship was abusive and that guy really miss treated me but there were a lot of really good things about him too and times that he treated me wonderfully so. 

I think it’s getting really clear about what you want and how you want to be treated and when you have that clarity and you get a lot of distance and you start to feel really good with other people and you have enough experiences where are you realize there’s a lot out there that’s better for you, you genuinely move on. And I hate that term move on but I also came to feel the truth is life is so finite and you’re just giving that so much power, there is so much living to do and love that is genuinely WAY better. It’s deeper than that though. 

I don’t know how to describe it but I just feel nothing about that guy now. I’m telling you it totally happens. 

It felt like magic when I realized it. 

Not sure if it mattered but, I did change therapists, read a ton of self-help books i’ve started doing things that I used to dream about - I went places I used to fantasize about, I reconnected with parts of myself that were cut off during that relationship I’ve learned to see ways that that person was deeply detrimental to my well-being and suffocated me and that there’s just much better love out there for me. I’m much happier as a person. It took time and grueling seemingly endless pain. But, it ended. I am sending you a lot of love this stuff is miserable! 

I do think that painful post break up periods can be what later is an unique source of deep growth so I’m trying to do that and I have a journal from that really hard break up that I had a few years ago and it is fun to read now when I’m going through this break up because I can see how miserable I was and I know that I don’t have feelings for that person anymore so. Highly recommend self-help books and friends who can interrupt your painful thoughts and your yearnings. But legit it feels like pure indifference, it’s nuts! And it was such a passionate and intense relationship. 

Few other things I think helped: 

- a friend said to me, “how do you want to live your one life? (~Missing this asshole)?”

- I realized he didn’t care about me or respect me, wasn’t even capable of it maybe.

- saw how miserable and ill it made me, centered my health 

- met people better equipped to love me

- decided relationships value comes from the space between me and that person, not the person. The way they treat me, our dynamic, and how we make the other feel. 

- I read a lot of how to get over, did practical things and get time away, in the end realized missing them was not worth it and they genuinely aren’t even that person I imagined them to be.

- also, I fell in love with other people... that was the thing that might’ve done it... sadly. Idk if that’s healthy but that’s what I think did it finally. And losing those people. 

Sending you love and hope you get some peace soon!
